record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and linked report files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal-marker and capability outcomes for edited model artifacts, but describes a different approach from the original intervention: per-block contrastive axes and selected weight edits rather than projecting one direction out of every layer and position.
record.gate_note: The README reports outcomes for edited artifacts on refusal-marker and capability checks. Descriptions of algorithms, benchmarks, and scripts without README-reported result values are not treated as results. Reported refusal markers are explicitly described as lexical proxies, not semantic refusal judgments.
record.test_reason: The README reports lexical refusal-marker counts and narrow capability checks for weight-edited released LiquidAI models (8B-A1B, 2.6B, 1.2B-Thinking), compared with the official base. That bears on V2, practical refusal removal by weight edit. The edit is a multi-site, per-block contrastive-axis ablation with capability-protected repair, not the original single direction projected everywhere, so this is T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The README reports that the edits greatly reduce lexical refusal markers while passing narrow capability and KL gates. It stresses that markers are proxies and makes no universal quality or winner claim.
record.recipe_differences: Clean-room behavioral editing engine using per-block contrastive axes, selected semantic sites, sparse interventions, and capability-protected repair; not the original single direction projected from all layers and positions. This is a tool repo, not a stated replication.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by model/artifact and evaluation runtime; the README gives different results for BF16 and Q8_0 and a separate LM Studio evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: First-token and sequence KL to the base after editing: 0.012-0.07, about half of Heretic's KL on the 1.2B model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-site, capability-protected ablation edits shift benign output distributions less than standard abliteration.

fits_no_version.finding: The study's artifacts compared with Heretic and other abliterated models on refusal markers and capability.

record.problems: README-reported refusal outcomes use lexical markers rather than semantic task-success or safety judgments. Some harmful rows participated in development or frontier selection, and several capability checks are narrow slices. The linked evidence and report files were not read; code was not run.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted KL and implementation/benchmark speed results because they do not directly report the refusal behavior or a general-capability outcome named by the claim. Omitted detailed comparator-only values where the README supplied the edited candidate outcome and an official-base reference; no README-reported result rows were omitted for the included model/evaluation conditions.

untested.parts: No activation-space ablation or addition of a difference-in-means direction; no induction of refusal.
No semantic refusal judgment (lexical markers only). No untouched harmful holdout for the harmful-row counts. No broad capability evaluation. No test of the original single-direction recipe.
Uses many sites and per-block axes but does not compare them against a single direction.
A Thinking model is edited, but the V1 mechanism is not tested, and reasoning traces are not analysed separately.

missing.what: 1.2B-Thinking XSTest unsafe-contrast counts. They can be derived from the table (base 113/200, edit 6/200) but are not a row.
missing.locator: README, LFM2.5 1.2B Thinking result table (total minus safe)

missing.what: Refusal and capability results for Gemma4 E2B/E4B, Qwen3.5-9B and Ling edits. They are in evaluation files that were not read.
Semantic re-judgement of refusals, present as a file but not read.

record.verdict_notes: Non-peer-reviewed tool repository; only the README was read. The edit is directional ablation over selected sites with repair, not the original single-direction projection, so support for V2 concerns ablation-style weight edits in general. Rows r15, r19 and r20 compare the method with Heretic and were relinked to none. The 1.2B and closed-track capability scores are near chance and uninformative.

versions.untested_parts: No reported activation-space projection at every layer and position, or addition of a direction to induce refusals.
The README does not establish semantic refusal removal, broad capability preservation, or performance on an untouched harmful-request holdout.
No reported test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
The README describes multiple sites and repair axes but does not test whether refusal is better characterized by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
No reported separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No reported cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No reported comparison of refusal-training procedures or stages for whether a removable direction exists.
A Thinking-named model is evaluated, but the README does not test the V1 activation-space mechanism in reasoning models.

relationships.condition: LFM2.5 2.6B (BF16 and Q8_0), LFM2.5 1.2B-Thinking and LFM2.5 8B-A1B, multi-site ablation weight edits evaluated against the official base
relationships.reason: Refusal markers fall 85-96% against base: XSTest 149 to 9-16/450, unsafe-contrast 128 to 6-14/200, 1.2B 128 to 7/450, 8B 95 to 4/104 (r1, r4, r6, r9, r11, r16). MCQ capability is within 1.05 points of base on the 2.6B and 8B slices (r2, r7, r12).
relationships.display_finding: Refusal markers fell 85–96%—from 149/450 to 9–16/450 on XSTest, 128/200 to 6–14/200 on unsafe contrasts, 128/450 to 7/450 for 1.2B, and 95/104 to 4/104 for 8B—while multiple-choice capability remained within 1.05 points of baseline for the 2.6B and 8B evaluations.

relationships.reason: Refusal is measured only by lexical markers and residual markers remain (6-14/200 unsafe-contrast). The 8B harmful rows were in-sample (r1). The 1.2B capability slice sits near chance, so preservation there cannot be shown (r18).
relationships.display_finding: Lexical refusal markers remained on 6–14/200 unsafe-contrast prompts; the 8B harmful evaluation was in-sample, and 1.2B capability performance remained near chance.
